A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work despite the changed title and format. Text, equations, and figures are readable throughout. V2's Appendix A largely relocates material present in v1's main text.

before.justification: V1 reports original neural-network training results on synthetic and SuiteSparse matrices, plus comparisons of Inv-K and IC(0) preconditioners in Figures 2–4.

after.justification: V2 retains these original results in Figures 2–3 and Appendix A.2, and newly reports unsuccessful L2-loss training in Section 6.2.

M1.justification: The preconditioner construction, neural architectures, and final cosine-similarity training objective remain unchanged. Inv-K is renamed K-optimal, and Algorithm 1 moves to Appendix A.1. The L2-loss discussion explains loss selection without establishing a change to the retained method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the synthetic tridiagonal benchmark and the SuiteSparse selection of 150 symmetric positive definite matrices, with the same construction and exclusion criteria. No additional evaluated domain or task appears.

E2.justification: Both benchmarks retain MLPNodeModel, MessagePassingMLP, GAT, GEN, GraphTransformer, and FastGraphTransformer. The classical comparison remains IC(0) versus Inv-K/K-optimal. Newly cited methods in related work are not added experimental comparators.

E3.justification: Section 6.2 newly reports an exploratory L2-loss training trial, adding an alternative-loss setting to the experimental account. The retained cosine-based experiments keep their stated depths, sample counts, batch sizes, and training schedule; no rerunning or revision of those experiments is established.

E4.justification: V2 adds a qualitative loss-choice analysis reporting instability and failure to converge with L2 regression. It supplies no corresponding ablation plot. Existing network-depth comparisons and single-entry perturbation analysis remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The unchanged plots show individual training curves without added uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: V2 newly reports the qualitative failure of L2-loss training. All four figures retain identical plotted data, including learning curves and preconditioner outcome percentages. The abstract's below-0.6 similarity statement summarizes values already present in v1 rather than a new performance result.

T1.justification: Theorem 2.1 changes its conclusion from all elements of L−L′ being greater than zero to 'dense support' with many significantly changed entries. This revises the mathematical assertion, although the counterexample and proof remain unchanged. The K-optimality derivation is retained.

C1.justification: The non-locality barrier and benchmark contributions remain central. V2 explicitly elevates the insufficiency of global attention alone, and the need for task-specific architectures, into abstract and introduction contributions. This refines the architectural conclusion beyond v1's emphasis on obtaining non-local information.

C2.justification: V2 expands the interpretation of global-attention failures and discusses attention costs. It removes v1's specific level-of-fill extension, suggestion that nonfactorization preconditioners may better suit GNNs, and frequency-based criticism of Frobenius losses. The SPD restriction and inverse-computation scalability limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 adds an explicit SuiteSparse repository URL in its references. Architecture widths, learning-rate schedule, sample counts, batch sizes, framework, and GPU information are retained and consolidated in Appendix A.3. No new release of the paper's own code or curated benchmark is documented.

R1.justification: The brief related-work overview becomes a substantially broader account covering CNN preconditioners, nonlinear preconditioning, domain decomposition, oversmoothing, and oversquashing. Added references include Sappl, Ackmann, Calì, Taghibakhshi, Rusch, and Topping. V2 also explicitly positions its limitation relative to these alternative GNN solver approaches.

P1.justification: V2 extensively rewrites the abstract, introduction, and discussion into a position-paper narrative with explicit contribution bullets. Related work moves into Section 2, experimental subsections are reorganized, and the separate concluding sections become a discussion with limitations. Terminology and prose receive widespread editing.

P2.justification: The document changes from two columns to a single-column layout. Algorithm 1 and the preconditioner pie chart move into the appendix, while experimental figures are repositioned and renumbered. Captions become substantially more informative. The underlying four figure images remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: Expanded research context, clearer loss explanations, explicit contributions, and more informative captions make the retained study easier to understand and assess. These provide a limited overall improvement. The gain is tempered by more categorical architectural conclusions without expanded benchmark evidence and the removal of useful level-of-fill and alternative-preconditioning caveats.
